synopsis: Lin Mo is a transmigrator who has spent three years as a menial disciple of Xuantian Sect, bullied, impoverished, and one failed assessment away from the mining pits, until the Deduction System binds to him on the brink of the Burial-Soul Abyss. Cornered by Zhang Kuang over a thousand-year Blood Jade Ginseng, he sacrifices the ginseng to the system instead of surrendering it, deduces his mortal Mountain-Opening Fist into a spirit-grade art, kills Zhang Kuang in a single blow, and absorbs the dead man's cultivation, Qiankun Bag, and a mysterious black bead. From that moment the lowest rung of the sect becomes his hunting ground: he slaughters demon beasts, completes dozens of missions in days, and forces his way into the outer sect, while the bead's inner world reveals a spatial node that points back to the Burial-Soul Abyss and a secret still waiting there. The story's first great crucible is the Huang Clan. Lin Mo saves Huang Ling'er from a pack of Rift Wind Wolves for a Minor Foundation Pill, then is drawn into a clan war: the Zhao Clan, led by the late-Foundation-Establishment Zhao Tianba and allied with the Blood Wolf Gang, has crippled Huang Zhenshan with a Profound Yin Sha Palm and seized the Huang estates. Hired to stall Zhao Tianba while the clan head recovers, Lin Mo blows up the Zhao outpost, flees through the woods carrying Huang Ling'er, survives a full-powered fireball through a spirit-grade body art, and kills Zhao Tianba after Huang Ling'er throws herself in front of a spear meant for him. The bead heals her mortal wound. In return Lin Mo receives a Foundation Pill, Cold Jade Marrow, and an alchemist's insight; a mysterious stone hidden inside the bead releases dragon blood, granting him a True Dragon bloodline, the Dragon Transformation divine ability, and a black hole in his dantian that tempers flesh and spirit. The black bead is then revealed by the system as the Mysterious Phoenix Bead, a damaged treasure of the Tianfeng Clan able to traverse star domains and purify bloodlines, and it awakens a jealous artifact spirit that demands demon cores and resents Lin Mo's growing romance. A system upgrade adds a lottery, detection, and divine ability derivation. Ten draws yield the Myriad Transformations Forbidden Dao Physique and an innate ability that multiplies his strength tenfold, plus the Wheel of Samsara Dao Fist, a technique beyond the world's peak. Lin Mo hunts Foundation Establishment beasts in the Hundred-Thousand Mountains, feeds the bead, and steals a Dragon Transformation Fruit from a Golden Core flood dragon, raising his True Dragon bloodline and escaping through Dragon Transformation. Back at Xuantian Sect he defeats Zhang De's revenge faction, including Zhou Sui, and is blackmailed by Xu Jiao, who knows he killed Zhang Kuang and the Cold Pool crocodile. He overpowers her and her brother, later gives her a Foundation Pill when her elder father has vanished in the Burial-Soul Abyss, and helps her break through during the outer sect tournament. By the close of this arc Lin Mo stands at Foundation Establishment seventh layer, armed with a spirit-grade high Mountain-Opening Fist, Swimming Dragon Step, Iron Bone Art, and the Wheel of Samsara Dao Fist, his body tempered by a supreme physique and True Dragon blood. He is bound to Huang Ling'er, entangled with Xu Jiao, trailed by a bead whose distant owners have sensed its awakening, and still facing Zhang De's vendetta and the secret of the Burial-Soul Abyss. The menial disciple has become something the sect can no longer ignore, and the road from the lowest rung to the evergreen way has only just begun.

Chen Yang transmigrates mid-meal into a misty wood and awakens the Lifewoven with Heaven System, which binds his lifespan to that of the local Heavenly Dao and lets him endure for tens of thousands of years, drawing on merit, lifespan and System rewards to outlast every enemy. What begins as a starving survivor raising an orphaned girl in a dying town becomes a long, irreverent pilgrimage through sects, kingdoms, realms and heavens. In the mortal arc he joins the Fuyao Sect, avenges its slaughtered disciples against the Qingyun Sect, and rises through the Yellow Turban wars beside Song Jiang, becoming the celebrated National Worthy of Great Shu. He takes Liu Jinyao under his wing, faces the Heavenly Derivation Sacred Body, and earns the title Son of the Heavenly Dao. But the System will not let him rest: rebirths, side quests and merit penalties keep dragging him from one crisis to the next, from the Buddhist realm's Tonsure Assembly and a Scripture Prison to the Warring States, where he must put the Ninth Prince Li Xuan on the throne with the aid of a Heavenly Dao System that hands out east winds and magical artifacts. The middle of the book turns on the Heavenly Dao itself. When a world's Dao loses balance and blackens, Chen Yang is tasked with eradicating it and recasting the Wenqu Sacred Light; he boils a Heavenly Dao to death, binds newborn ones like the child Tou Tian, and even slaps and scolds gods who presume to judge him. He accumulates evergreen vines and lifespan by the hundred million years, resurrects allies with cards and pills, and moves between the Immortal Realm, the Celestial Court and the Underworld with the same shameless, food-obsessed swagger. Over nine hundred and fifty chapters the final movements pit him against the full machinery of heaven: Sun Wukong and the Celestial Court, Erlang Shen, Nezha, Guanyin, the Jade Emperor, Taishang Laojun and the Queen Mother of the West, then the Ten Kings of the Underworld and the rules of reincarnation written in red spider lilies. Throughout, the opposition is rarely a single villain; it is procedure, inherited habit, corrupt clans, and competent people doing their work, all running on a Heavenly Dao that Chen Yang intends to outlive. The reader watches a slacker who wanted only to eat and lie flat learn, across millennia, to use what he knows and to stop treating usefulness as authority, while never quite giving up the right to complain to the System.

Ning Yan is seventeen and two tokens short of a winter roster on Coldwater Ridge: an outer-court labourer with a right hand that closes only halfway, who has filled the hours column four hundred times without moving a mark of her own. She copies ledgers for merit that never accrues to her, and the only thing she has ever been good at is reading a column of figures without thinking. The voice that wakes in her head belongs to a cultivator killed at nineteen on the stones below the Ash Gate for a core worth taking. He has woken inside the announcement layer of the world itself: no body, no hands, able to read every living cultivator as an account, to name one person Chosen, and to set quests in her head that the world will honour. He sets the Price himself, and always the cheapest available. He can speak to one person, and he chooses her. He is her brother, and the spending of what he does costs him the room he died in, the word his mother called him by, and most of his sister's face; he can still read her page like a clerk reads a ledger, and can no longer speak to her or hear her. Nothing obliges her to obey him. He keeps her alive by keeping her small; she is the one climbing. One of them has to stop. When she takes a Core at the Ash Gate she becomes a lamp: her account opens and every breath writes her larger, readable from forty feet away, while her pool burns down to a coal and her arms hang dead. She rebuilds in an infirmary shed and a copying room, learning that a quest is never free. A witnessed claim displaces the nearest turn that contradicts it; a repair convoy never leaves, a route a district can no longer choose, a harvest or a message or an evacuation another family was going to make for itself. The cost is never refunded, and a false claim spends before it rebounds. The opposition is institutional and sincere: a deacon whose private book decides postings, readers who examine her in closed rooms, a factor who puts her on the flat half, copyists who keep a district's figures, and a brother who would rather she stay unkillable than be seen. What the reader watches is a labourer with a half-working hand learn to publish uncertainty before she acts instead of after, and to keep accounts out loud rather than privately: fair copies read at gate stones before witnesses, held rooms, verification grounds, roads and towns and counters, letters to a brother she is still lying to inside true sentences. She gathers the people the arithmetic left out — a water-carrier who will not be forgotten, an old reader on two sticks, a factor who judges by eye, a deacon who keeps his own line — and learns that a correct forecast is also a political act. The last movement turns on whether a country facing its worst convergence will be handed one final answer, or whether the people living inside the forecast will be asked to choose; on whether a town that has been lent a sentence will hear it in the mouth it came from; and on a sister and a brother who can no longer speak to each other, one of whom has to stop.

Jiang Lin has a Game System, a lunch tray, a school uniform, and a carefully cultivated habit of being forgettable. Then a red light takes him off a school roof and drops him into a forest of screaming strangers. The Loop World introduces itself: mission worlds, protection quests, elimination runs, faction wars, and a reward shop that accepts only exchange points. Everyone else sees a quiet student with no weapons and no team. Jiang Lin sees levels, loot, and a game he has already cleared in another life. He is the System made flesh: a body that runs on hit points, a private stat sheet, an aim that locks on, and a fear response switched off like a status effect. The mission worlds are his dungeons, and he runs them like a man who has read the book—rescue the lost girl, farm the goblins, turn a zombie siege into a harvest, choose the losing side of a martial-arts war because he knows how it ends. The first mission leaves most of the strangers dead and a perfect rating in his log. The missions pay him in levels and exchange points. The Loop World collects the rest—sometimes in the lives of strangers who trusted him, always in another piece of the ordinary world. The bill is never in HP. He can still laugh, eat, and want; the System just makes sure he never has to feel the weight. He tells himself every face that survives the run is a witness, a liability, or bait. He spends his points on a bloodline, spellbooks, and crafting skills, then builds a shop out of what he makes. The Loop World is full of people who have learned the same arithmetic: team captains with bloodlines and body counts, veterans who treat newcomers as walking shields, rival Loopers who would rather kill a promising rookie than let him grow. Fang Xinyi, the school's Ice Beauty, transfers into his department to stand closer to him. Between missions he goes back to class, sells potions online, and pretends she is just another classmate. Gao Wen, an actress who runs a team of her own, offers him a seat at her table. Neither woman is content to watch from the sidelines. He refuses every team that asks, Blood Rose included, and sells them enchanted bullets instead. A man with a secret that big cannot afford witnesses, so Jiang Lin keeps his distance. But the missions are getting harder, the teams are learning what he can do, and the Loop World does not care how clever a player is. It only cares whether he comes back. The rest is just noise.

Jiang Lin is a high school student who wakes one day with a Game System welded to his soul: a stat sheet, lock-on aim, item drops, and a warehouse that never fills. When the red light takes him into his first Loop Instance, a goblin dungeon with a protection mission and a lost girl in a cage, he is the only newcomer who treats the whole thing as a game to be farmed. He kills the boss, earns the first SSS rating anyone has ever seen, and walks out with over ten thousand exchange points while the veterans who underestimated him are left wondering what hit them. Back in the real world he keeps the System a secret, sells enchanted bullets and life skills through an online shop, and quietly becomes self-sufficient. Fang Xinyi, the ice-beauty classmate who lent him a pistol without hesitation, transfers departments to stay near him and joins the all-female Blood Rose team under the superstar Gao Wen. Jiang Lin refuses to join any team — only the weak band together, he says — but he is happy to trade: points for services, services for points, with a bottom line that is simply whether he feels like it. His second instance is a jiangshi world, and this is where the book shows what he really is. Reading the plot in advance, he feeds three veterans and a crowd of newcomers to a single evolving corpse, turns the town into a feeding ground, and then calls down a lightning blade to harvest the experience himself. He leaves with a hundred and fifty thousand points, the Saiyan bloodline, and a book of Maoshan arts that Uncle Nine, a Daoist whose level even the System cannot read, presses into his hands. From those pages he learns divination, talismans, soul communication and the rest, and the System folds them into new functions, including a threat value that tells him exactly how much danger anyone in the room represents. The third instance drops him into the world of the Heavenly Sword and Dragon Sabre, on the Ming Cult's side. By now he can swallow an entire barrage and return it with borrowed force, drain a Wolverine-blooded Looper dry in an endless cycle of absorption and regeneration, and force whole teams to surrender rather than face him. He takes the Qiankun Great Shift, a night in the secret chamber with Zhou Zhiruo, and another six-figure haul of points, and uses them to buy a spellbook of time and space. Fused with the Maoshan arts, it becomes [World]: a twenty-cubic-metre field where he is the Five Elements, the direction, and time itself. By then Jiang Lin is no longer a newcomer. He is the supernova the Abyss Forum cannot stop talking about, a cheater whose kill counts and ratings make veteran captains go pale. The opposition is rarely a monster. It is procedure and arrogance: teams that believe their numbers and their trump cards make them safe, a captain with an Archangel token who can resurrect his dead, and the state Looper agency, Guaranteed Arrival, whose white-haired old man sends a girl to make contact because the Corrosion is getting worse and they are short of people. Jiang Lin does not care about any of it. He lives for himself, keeps the two worlds separate, and treats every instance as a harvest he planted with his own hands. What the reader watches is a man learning that the only thing more dangerous than a Loop World is a man who has decided that every world in it is his farm: the ice beauty who follows him like a lovesick fool, the superstar who cannot decide whether to recruit him or buy from him, the veterans who discover too late that surrender is not always on the menu, and a boy with a System who keeps leveling up while everyone else is still trying to survive.

Ye Qiu has lived as an omnipotent System across millions of years, lodging in the bodies of doomed heroes and forging legends, but even an emperor of three thousand Great Emperors has never broken the final shackle above the Heavenly Emperor. Casting off the System's body, he reincarnates into flesh and blood, weak and unable to cultivate, and begins again from nothing. His first act is to return to the Confucian Saint Academy as the long-awaited Confucian Emperor: the statue of the sage kneels, the Hundred-Aperture Literary Heart returns to him, and all the talent under heaven is drawn into a single vortex before being scattered back as a blessing that remakes scholars, sages, and a chancellor alike. Then, having opened heaven with a single stroke, he leaves. His body is too frail for the road ahead, so he seeks the primordial blood of the City of Astonishment, the lawless city he once founded as the Heaven-Defying Demon God Yu Jingtian. There the Dian family, faithful to him for a hundred thousand years, has been ground down by the Feng, Huo and Lei families, their blood pool seized and their patriarch Dian Haoran left dying. Ye Qiu crushes the three families' elites with a clench of his hand, restores Dian Haoran with a Sacred Demon Blood Pill, and leaves Jingtian City in the hands of the one general who never betrayed him. From there he goes to Qingqiu, where the Nine-Tailed Fox clan has withered under the Divine Court. He finds a descendant named Qianqian, a remnant soul of the Empress Bai Qianqian hidden inside a girl, and the Left Eye of Heaven sealed beneath a mountain. He gathers an army of remnants, tears open the Divine Court branch, and when the Stone Demon King hides his soul inside half a million civilians Ye Qiu turns the Left Eye of Heaven on them and on the arriving Stone Emperor, burning through the Chaotic Immortal Fetus and Soul he has just nurtured to do it. Among the ruins he frees Sun Wukong from the Five-Fingered Mountain, takes the monkey as a disciple, and walks west through a Buddhist land whose temples are built on the toil of the faithful, drawing on the power beneath it to break the seals that hold the world's Buddhist energy captive. What the reader watches is not a stronger man deciding everything, but an old emperor learning to be mortal again: cultivating the Primordial Immortal Canon, nurturing a Chaotic Immortal Fetus and Soul against his own demonic blood, and paying for every advance in memory, blood and breath. The opposition is never a single villain with a face; it is institutions that classify, offices that prune, and faithful people who have read the same figures and come out differently. The last movement asks whether a man who has been the answer for ten million lives can stop being the only one who decides.
